title: Document linux system dependencies
description:
The first thing I do with a new R install is reaching out for the tidyverse, but installing it on Linux is always an adventure. Let's remember that [tidyverse.org](tidyverse.org) and [tidyverse.tidyverse.org](tidyverse.tidyverse.org) just say:

`install.packages("tidyverse")`

On linux this almost always fails, because individual packages have system dependencies that can't be resolved by `install.packages`. This is well known, for example #339 or #325 just to mention two issues in this repo, and affects several distros (Ubuntu and Fedora at least, that I know of).
This wouldn't be a big deal if it wasn't that the console output running the install command above isn't very helpful. One needs to try one tidyverse package at a time, scan the output of those install looking for the missing system libraries, and keep going until all of them are solved.

I have gone through this process a few times already, but I still don't know exactly which libraries are required to install the tidyverse. I understand that there might be some variation from one distro to another, but it would be very helpful to have these dependencies documented somewhere easy to find, so one can check what's already installed and what's required beforehand. Thank you.

EDIT: I remembered that [this thread](https://forum.posit.co/t/cant-install-tidyverse-on-posit-workbench-ubuntu/170850) suggests using [packagemanager.posit.co](packagemanager.posit.co) to find these dependencies, and it seems to do a great work! Maybe a reference to this, telling how to set the distribution and check the "Install System Prerequisites" would be enough.

title: Declaring attached packages in DESCRIPTION
description:
Starting with https://github.com/posit-dev/ark/pull/870, our LSP detects which packages are attached by `library()` calls based on installed files. When a package depends on other packages on the search path, this is usually declared in the `Depends:` field in DESCRIPTION. For the {tidyverse} package that field is empty, I assume to avoid conflicts with `library()`'s own auto-attach behaviour.

For now I've hard-coded the list of packages attached with tidyverse and tidymodels. In the longer term though we need a new DESCRIPTION field to declare the list of packages attached from `.onAttach()`. This could look like:

```dcf
Config/Needs/attach: dplyr, readr, forcats, stringr, ggplot2, tibble, lubridate, tidyr, purrr
```

title: Feature Request: Option to Update All Tidyverse Packages to GitHub Development Versions
description:
**Description:**
I'd like to propose adding a function or utility in the tidyverse package that allows users to easily update all (or selected) tidyverse packages to their latest development versions from GitHub.

**Motivation:**
In many cases, individual tidyverse packages have valuable updates or bug fixes in their development versions well before they're released on CRAN. For example, a recent tibble development update fixed `view()` issues ([tibble#1603](https://github.com/tidyverse/tibble/pull/1603)) in Positron — a fix not yet available in the CRAN version.

When switching devices or reverting temporarily to CRAN versions (e.g. for environments like R-WASM), it becomes time-consuming and error-prone to manually reinstall multiple tidyverse packages from GitHub.

I tried the following but it didn't work as I expected:

``` r
library(tidyverse)

tidyverse_update(recursive = TRUE, repos = "https://tidyverse.r-universe.dev")
#> Error in pkgs[pkg_deps, "Version"]: subscript out of bounds
```


```r
tidyverse_install_dev(core_only = TRUE)
```

title: tidyverse installation fail on MacOS 10.11.6 el capitan
description:
Hello,

I am currently in the process of installing the tidyverse package on my MacOS 10.11.6 system. I have R version 3.6.3 and R Studio version 1.1.463, which are both the latest versions compatible with my operating system.

Despite my efforts, I have encountered persistent failures in attempting to install tidyverse. Upon analyzing the error messages, it appears that the issue is related to the age of my operating system. Specifically, a crucial dependency known as "systemfonts" necessitates a .o file from MacOS 10.13, a version newer than my current 10.11.

This incompatibility has resulted in error messages similar to the one provided below:

```r
ld: warning: object file (/private/var/folders/fr/myfcbqmj1lz2lbklhxkr1s5c0000gn/T/RtmpqdxJab/R.INSTALL472a67fa289e/systemfonts/.deps/lib/libpng.a(pngwio.o)) was built for newer OSX version (10.13) than being linked (10.11)
```

Your willingness to assist is greatly appreciated. Your guidance could encompass methods for bypassing the dependency, procuring a pre-compiled tidyverse package for binary installation, or acquiring the necessary .o files that are currently absent on my system. Your support is invaluable. Thank you!

title: Extraneous `tidyverse_conflicts()` for re-exported functions
description:
`tidyverse::tidyverse_conflicts()` gives what I think is an extraneous conflict between `dplyr::filter()` and  `simpr::filter()`, even though `simpr::filter()` is just a re-export of the generic S3 method of `dplyr::filter()`.

``` r
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(simpr))
library(tidyverse)
packageVersion("tidyverse")
#> [1] '1.3.1.9000'
tidyverse_conflicts()
#> ── Conflicts ────────────────────────────────────────── tidyverse_conflicts() ──
#> x dplyr::filter() masks simpr::filter(), stats::filter()
#> x dplyr::lag()    masks stats::lag()
```

<sup>Created on 2022-03-19 by the [reprex package](https://reprex.tidyverse.org) (v2.0.1)</sup>

I expected `tidyverse_conflicts()` to only flag the conflict with `stats::filter()`. The `simpr` package has many other re-exports of `dplyr` methods, but for some reason only `filter()` shows up in `tidyverse_conflicts()`.

title: Consider adding `rticulate/import`?
description:

Asked the author [1], and was given the impression that the author won't object to be included in `tidyverse`. Would tidyverse consider including a solution like this?

This is standard in many languages, such as Haskell, Python, Go, ...

[1] https://github.com/rticulate/import/issues/24

title: Move `master` branch to `main`
description:
The `master` branch of this repository will soon be renamed to `main`, as part of a coordinated change across several GitHub organizations (including, but not limited to: [tidyverse](https://github.com/tidyverse), [r-lib](https://github.com/r-lib), [tidymodels](https://github.com/tidymodels), and [sol-eng](https://github.com/sol-eng)). We anticipate this will happen by the end of September 2021.

That will be preceded by a release of the [usethis package](https://usethis.r-lib.org), which will gain some functionality around detecting and adapting to a renamed default branch. There will also be a blog post at the time of this `master` --> `main` change.

The purpose of this issue is to:

* Help us firm up the list of targetted repositories
* Make sure all maintainers are aware of what's coming
* Give us an issue to close when the job is done
* Give us a place to put advice for collaborators re: how to adapt

*message id: euphoric_snowdog*

title: programming problem with {{ var }}
description:
Brief description of the problem

Function in dplyr with {{var }} is not working as expected. Here is a comparison b/w 2 functions using {{}} and !!. 

```r
# Func using embracing {{ }}:
sum_grp <- function(df, grpVar, sumvar) {
  
  res <- df %>%
    group_by({{ grpVar }}) %>%
    summarise(
      n =n(),
      mean = mean({{ sumvar }}, na.rm = T)
    )
}

# Func with bang  !!:

sum_grp2 <- function(df, grpVar, sumvar) {
  
  grpVar = sym(grpVar)
  sumvar = sym(sumvar)
  
  res <- df %>%
    group_by(!!grpVar) %>%
    summarise(
      n =n(),
      mean = mean(!!sumvar, na.rm = T)
    )
}

# Testing with data

df1 = data.frame(cls = 'A', val = 1:10)
df2 = data.frame(cls = 'B', val = 1:10+10)
df = bind_rows(df1,df2)

# embracing: wrong results 
(sum_grp(df, grpVar = 'cls', sumvar = 'val'))
# A tibble: 1 x 3
  `"cls"`     n  mean
  <chr>   <int> <dbl>
1 cls        20    NA
Warning message:
In mean.default(~"val", na.rm = T) :
  argument is not numeric or logical: returning NA

# bang: correct results
(sum_grp2(df, grpVar = 'cls', sumvar = 'val'))
# A tibble: 2 x 3
  cls       n  mean
  <chr> <int> <dbl>
1 A        10   5.5
2 B        10  15.5

```
My version: dplyr 1.0.7

title: List all authors in the text version of the citation
description:
In `inst/CITATION`, the text version of the citation truncates the author list with "et al.". 

How about including the full list of authors? It's standard in some formats to truncate author lists above 6. But more and more allow for large author lists. And it's simple to manually replace the authors with "et al." if someone wants to.




title: Time to rename the ‘master’ branch of all repos?
description:
As you are probably well aware, GitHub [has been initialising](https://github.com/github/renaming) new repositories with the more inclusive and neutral branch name `main` instead of `master` since October 1, 2020. By doing so, GiHub follows the statements and actions [as stated by Git and the Software Freedom Conservancy in June 2020](https://sfconservancy.org/news/2020/jun/23/gitbranchname/). 

I noticed that RStudio ([github.com/rstudio/rstudio](https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio)) has already renamed their main branch to `main`, and [also clearly states why](https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/blob/main/README.md).

So, will tidyverse follow? All of it? Please do 🙂

title: Encoding issue with symbol U+221A
description:
When English R locale is used, no issue is present, when Lithuanian (Latvian, etc.) R locale is used (which is the default on my PC), there symbol `√` (`U+221A`) is displayed incorrectly.
These are the results in a fresh R session:

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/12725868/108633332-612c6c00-747c-11eb-8911-e4f17597722b.png)

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/12725868/108633358-87520c00-747c-11eb-9076-91d6ca382c1d.png)

I use R on Windows 10. I think this issue is Windows-specific. 


1) Could this encoding issue be solved for the Lithuanian, Latvian, etc. locales?
2) If not, could the symbol `U+221A` be replaced with the letter `v`?

title: "subscript out of bounds" error when loading tidyverse
description:
After a fresh install on Debian Linux (R 3.5.2), I get the following error when loading tidyverse for the first time:

```
> library(tidyverse)
Error: package or namespace load failed for ‘tidyverse’:
 .onAttach failed in attachNamespace() for 'tidyverse', details:
  call: clienv$num_colors[[std]]
  error: subscript out of bounds
```

The install of tidyverse looked clean, including the load test at the end.

title: Document system dependencies
description:
## Short summary

Document system dependencies like curl or openssl and how to install to them, so especially new users can install them right before installing tidyverse, which makes the whole installation process easier.

## Problem description

When installing tidyverse, some system dependencies like curl or openssl are needed. If these are not installed, the tidyverse installation process fails:

```
------------------------- ANTICONF ERROR ---------------------------
Configuration failed because libcurl was not found. Try installing:
 * deb: libcurl4-openssl-dev (Debian, Ubuntu, etc)
 * rpm: libcurl-devel (Fedora, CentOS, RHEL)
 * csw: libcurl_dev (Solaris)
If libcurl is already installed, check that 'pkg-config' is in your
PATH and PKG_CONFIG_PATH contains a libcurl.pc file. If pkg-config
is unavailable you can set INCLUDE_DIR and LIB_DIR manually via:
R CMD INSTALL --configure-vars='INCLUDE_DIR=... LIB_DIR=...'
```

or

```
--------------------------- [ANTICONF] --------------------------------
Configuration failed because openssl was not found. Try installing:
 * deb: libssl-dev (Debian, Ubuntu, etc)
 * rpm: openssl-devel (Fedora, CentOS, RHEL)
 * csw: libssl_dev (Solaris)
 * brew: openssl@1.1 (Mac OSX)
If openssl is already installed, check that 'pkg-config' is in your
PATH and PKG_CONFIG_PATH contains a openssl.pc file. If pkg-config
is unavailable you can set INCLUDE_DIR and LIB_DIR manually via:
R CMD INSTALL --configure-vars='INCLUDE_DIR=... LIB_DIR=...
```

Users may be confused with these errors (see #225) and even if they understand what to do, the installation process is split into several parts as you have to install the needed packages (e.g. via APT) and then continue the tidyverse installation.

## Suggested change

Document the installation of needed system dependencies, e.g.:

```
apt install libcurl4-openssl-dev libssl-dev # ... maybe more? maybe libxml2-dev, see #243
```

Of course, installation with rpm, csw and brew should also be documented.

title: Dates, inequalities and infinite values printing as NA.
description:
I've got a question about the intended behavior of printing dates that were created through inequalities.  For example, I create some data here such that the variable `date` is a date with one missing value and I create `date2` such that it is the minimum value of `date` when `x` is bigger than 3.  There are no such instances in the first value of `group` in the data and the warning is printed that `Inf` is being returned as a result, which seems reasonable enough.  However, in the example below, you can see that these dates that were returned as `Inf` print as `NA` just as the original `NA` date did.  Further, these printed `NA` values don't evaluate to `TRUE` when `is.na()` is invoked.  Is this intended, or is there a way to have them print as `Inf` in the output? 

```{r}
tib <- tibble::tibble(
  x = c(1,2,3,4,5,6), 
  date = lubridate::as_date(c("1994-04-01", "1994-04-02",
                              "1994-04-01", "1994-04-02",
                              "1994-04-01", NA)), 
  group = c(1,1,2,2,3,3))
tib <- tib %>% 
  group_by(group) %>% 
  mutate(date2 = min(date[which(x > 3)], na.rm=TRUE))
# Warning messages:
# 1: Problem with `mutate()` input `date2`.
# ℹ no non-missing arguments to min; returning Inf
# ℹ Input `date2` is `min(date[which(x > 3)], na.rm = TRUE)`.
# ℹ The error occurred in group 1: group = 1. 
# 2: In min.default(numeric(0), na.rm = TRUE) :
#   no non-missing arguments to min; returning Inf

tib
# # A tibble: 6 x 4
# # Groups:   group [3]
#         x date       group date2     
#     <dbl> <date>     <dbl> <date>    
# 1     1 1994-04-01     1 NA        
# 2     2 1994-04-02     1 NA        
# 3     3 1994-04-01     2 1994-04-02
# 4     4 1994-04-02     2 1994-04-02
# 5     5 1994-04-01     3 1994-04-01
# 6     6 NA             3 1994-04-01

is.na(tib$date)
# [1] FALSE FALSE FALSE FALSE FALSE  TRUE
is.na(tib$date2)
# [1] FALSE FALSE FALSE FALSE FALSE FALSE
```

title: problem with dplyr::filter
description:
I have a df of timestamps and of ids. There are multiple timestamps pr Id, 

I want to filter the df by a date and then keep one unique ID.

However, I get the wrong results when I put the two requirements into the same filter compared with if I pipe the result into a new filter()

The result is sometimes the same so I have made a loop to run the comparisson 500 times. I find that the result is only identical about 100 times out of 500. (i'm struggeling to get consistent results with set.seed, so I used this quirky approach).

I'm running dplyr 1.0.2 with R: 4.0.2

I guess that the result should be the same always?

```r
num <- 1000
count <- 0
for(i in 1:500){

library(magrittr)
x <- tibble::tibble(
  id = LETTERS[rbinom(num, 25, 0.50)+1],
  timestamp = Sys.Date() - rbinom(num, 180, 0.50))

x1 <- x %>% 
  dplyr::filter(
    timestamp < as.Date("2020-08-01"),
    !duplicated(id))

x2 <- x %>% 
  dplyr::filter(
    timestamp < as.Date("2020-08-01")) %>% 
  dplyr::filter(
    !duplicated(id))

if(isTRUE(dplyr::all_equal(x1, x2))) count <- count+1

}
```

title: Feature idea for filter and drop_na alternative
description:
Previous scoped versions of the filter function allowed `any_vars` and `all_vars` aggregation logic. Now it just does the implicit equivalent of `all_vars`. Isn't it an idea to include an argument for this logic parameter in `filter` ? Default to "all" to preserve behavior, and allow "any" so users don't need to write row-wise helper functions.

E.g:

```r
filter(across(everything(), ~ !is.na(.x)), logic = "any") # Keep rows with any valid/non-NA value
```

Currently, to do the above using `across` scoping requires defining an additional rowAny function (see [here](https://stackoverflow.com/a/62829853/4627134)).

In a similar vein, since functions like `filter` and `select` expect the user to phrase the expression in terms of what they want to _keep_, it seems `drop_na` has the opposite mental approach. Wouldn't it be more consistent to have something like `complete_cases` where the user optionally selects the variable subset that needs to be complete?

E.g:

```r
df %>% complete_cases(outcome, all_of(predictor_vars)) # Drop rows our model can't use, but we don't care if other variables have NA values
```

title: Include rio into tidyverse
description:
Based on tidyverse's own list of packages for [importing/exporting files](https://www.tidyverse.org/packages/#import), I think it is pretty clear that the R environment lacks an intuitive way of import/export of files, in particular for the beginner. Having to know which package, and also the exact function name for a particular file type, and then all the various forms for argument names is unnecessary. The [`rio`-package](https://github.com/leeper/rio) is the equivalent of the broom-package for files by using a single function (`import()`/`export()`) across all data files. It is very intuitive, follows tidyverse-philosophy, allows returning tibbles, and makes it a breeze to work with files. I do not understand why this is seemingly kept out in the cold. (I am not a rio-developer so I have no personal interests to disclose). 
So why bother? Locating it among other tidyverse packages will attract users and developers, and set certain expectations for the upstream package developers in the same way as broom sets expectations about what kind of functions all model-objects should return.
If you let me going on a relevant rant: I sometimes think that the R-community's perhaps biggest weakness is that there are generally extrinsic and intrinsic incentives to start packages, but rarely any incentives for contributing to existing packages. (Try applying for funding from a research agency for _contributing_ to a package that lacks helpers, rather than starting something new). Although a certain level of competition and free choice is useful, it can actually hinder growth if people just see chaos.

description:
I am note sure if this is the right place to ask.

Some packages in the tidyverse are starting to throw error conditions with proper S3 classes, but very few other R packages do this. It would be nice to have base error classes along with guidance on when they should be used, like the [built-in exceptions](https://docs.python.org/3/library/exceptions.html) of python. Arguably, this is something that should be provided by base R, but the chances for that are slim in the near future. I was wondering if the tidyverse could provide something like this as a package.

title: Option to sort/arrange names_from in pivot_wider
description:
Consider the following example:

```
library(tidyverse)

tibble(
  X = c(1, 1, 2, 2),
  Y = letters[4:1],
  Z = 10 * 1:4
) %>% pivot_wider(
  names_from = Y,
  values_from = Z
)

```

This yields the output

```
# A tibble: 2 x 5
      X     d     c     b     a
  <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl>
1     1    10    20    NA    NA
2     2    NA    NA    30    40
```

An option `names_arrange = TRUE` (say, default is `FALSE`) would yield something similar to

```
library(tidyverse)

tibble(
  X = c(1, 1, 2, 2),
  Y = letters[4:1],
  Z = 10 * 1:4
) %>% arrange(
  Y
) %>% pivot_wider(
  names_from = Y,
  values_from = Z
)

# A tibble: 2 x 5
      X     a     b     c     d
  <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl>
1     2    40    30    NA    NA
2     1    NA    NA    20    10
```

title: Feature Request: tidyverse_conflicts() message with "conflicted Package Info"
description:
It would be nice, and easily implementable, that when executing tidyverse_conflicts() function, a message is also included that "spreads the word" about "conflicted" R Package, as an alternative (and useful) conflict resolution strategy.

Current behavior is:

```
> library(tidyverse)
-- Attaching packages --------------------------------------- tidyverse 1.3.0 --
v ggplot2 3.2.1     v purrr   0.3.3
v tibble  2.1.3     v dplyr   0.8.3
v tidyr   1.0.0     v stringr 1.4.0
v readr   1.3.1     v forcats 0.4.0
-- Conflicts ------------------------------------------ tidyverse_conflicts() --
x dplyr::filter() masks stats::filter()
x dplyr::lag()    masks stats::lag()
```

My proposal is:
```
-- Conflicts ------------------------------------------ tidyverse_conflicts() --
x dplyr::filter() masks stats::filter()
x dplyr::lag()    masks stats::lag()
-- Strict Conflict Resolution Strategy: Use 'conflicted' R Package for making every conflict between loaded package functions an error, and force you to choose which function to use.
```
Or:
```
-- Conflicts ------------------------------------------ tidyverse_conflicts() --
x dplyr::filter() masks stats::filter()
x dplyr::lag()    masks stats::lag()
-- For a Strict Conflict Resolution Strategy: Use 'conflicted' R Package.
```

title: Filter operation doesn't work if variable name intersects with column name
description:
**TL;DR:**
Using variable names that conflict with dataframe column names in a filter operation, doesn't yield expected results. 

**Example:**
I have a dataframe with a column named `week` which is a datatype of `<date>`. I run a filter such as:

`df_subset <- df %>% filter(week == "2019-08-26")`

Works just fine. Subsets data to those observations. However, if I run:

```
week <- "2019-08-26"
df_subset <- df %>% filter(week == week)
```

it does not subset at all. If I change my variable name to say, `w` it then works.

If it's not possible to permit the use of variable names that intersect with colum names in the tibble, I'd recommend at minimum, logging a warning.

title: a note on technology choices for the tidyverse paper
description:
Under the Philosophy section of the tidyverse paper, it might benefit from something like:

> The original goal of the S language was "to turn ideas into software, quickly and faithfully" (Chambers, 1998). To this end, the tidyverse eschews more sophisticated technologies that detract from the user's experience.

(This could use some word smithing)

I'm mostly thinking of things like S4 and R6 that are arguably superior CS methods for OOP but have a negative net effect on users. I would also hold up quasiquotation as a counter-example of something more complex that, due to its effect on interfaces, is a plus for users

title: Remove messages when loading tidyverse
description: When running `library(tidyverse)`, the default behavior is to print the packages loaded and a condensed summary of conflicts. However, particularly for `.Rmd` documents, the most common consequence of this behavior *for the user* is to add `message=FALSE` to the `R` chunk. Therefore, removing the message would decrease the amount of typing required of users. Users wanting the information could still use `tidyverse::tidyverse_conflicts()`.

title: tidyverse attaches its children packages at `pos=2`
description:
This is not really a bug but this is annoying, at least to me, I would expect it to attach them just before `tidyverse` on the search path.

I don't imagine a situation where someone would want to put `tidyverse` at `pos = 3` and then place the other packages at `pos = 2`. If you believe it would be a less common use case than mine, please consider adapting the behavior.

```
search()
# [1] ".GlobalEnv"        "tools:rstudio"     "package:stats"    
# [4] "package:graphics"  "package:grDevices" "package:utils"    
# [7] "package:datasets"  "package:methods"   "Autoloads"        
# [10] "package:base" 

something <- list()
attach(something)
library(tidyverse,pos = 3)
search()
# [1] ".GlobalEnv"        "package:forcats"   "package:stringr"  
# [4] "package:dplyr"     "package:purrr"     "package:readr"    
# [7] "package:tidyr"     "package:tibble"    "package:ggplot2"  
# [10] "something"         "package:tidyverse" "tools:rstudio"    
# [13] "package:stats"     "package:graphics"  "package:grDevices"
# [16] "package:utils"     "package:datasets"  "package:methods"  
# [19] "Autoloads"         "package:base" 
```

FYI I posted a SO question on how to handle this situation, so your inputs are welcome here or there too! 

https://stackoverflow.com/questions/52892704/how-to-reorder-the-search-path

title: Attach lubridate
description:
From @hadley on the [RStudio Discourse](https://community.rstudio.com/t/what-is-the-core-tidyverse-packages/3628/7?u=hammer) in January 2018:

> The real question is why isn’t lubridate in core? The answer is that it currently conflicts (in a narrow sense) with too many base functions - in practice the lubridate functions extend or wrap the base alternatives so the conflict aren’t harmful in practice, but I haven’t had time to think through how this should be indicated in the tidyverse loading screen.

Figured I'd file an issue on GitHub in case there's any loading screen progress to track (that could perhaps be linked to this issue).

title: Trouble installing tidyverse on macOS 10.13.4 (High Sierra) - solved by xcode-select --install
description:
1. Uninstall all versions of R and RStudio from MacBook Air.
2. Upgrade to macOS 10.13.4 (High Sierra).
3. Install RStudio 1.1.456.
4. `which r` from command line finds nothing (so I believe there are no conflicting version of R in play).
5. Launch RStudio.
6. `install.packages("tidyverse")` in RStudio fails trying to install `xml2` because `libxml-2.0` is not found.
7. `brew install libxml2` from command line does not fix the problem.
8. Run `xcode-select --install` from the command line (see <https://stackoverflow.com/questions/50229781/package-installation-in-r-fail-on-macos>).
9. Run `brew install libxml2`.
10. Re-launch RStudio, re-run `install.packages("tidyverse")` - installs `xml2` and then tells me `tidyverse` is installed. (Warns me that `default/America/Toronto` is an unknown timezone, but I can live with that...)
11. `library(tidyverse)` does what <http://r4ds.had.co.nz/data-visualisation.html> tells me I should expect.

See also #70 (maybe?).

title: Tidyverse startup message causes pdf output with pdflatex to fail
description:
The following document fails to compile in rstudio using default settings. The error message is `Package inputenc Error: Unicode char √ (U+221A)`.

 ```
     ---
     output: pdf_document
     ---
     a
     ```
     library(tidyverse)  
     ```
```
There are several workarounds:
* `options(tidyverse.quiet=TRUE)`
* chunk option `include=FALSE`
* `latex_engine: xelatex` (pdflatex is the default in rstudio)

However, I'm struggling to understand why all of this is necessary. Why does the startup message need to use unicode? Why doesn't tidyverse respect the `library(quietly=TRUE)` option?

If the startup behavior remains unchanged, shouldn't the documentation mention this issue prominently? (Just to be clear, this is not a hypothetical issue, this caused ongoing problems in a class I taught using tidyverse. I had no idea where the unicode was coming from.)

title: Duplicate listing of package listing from library(tidyverse) if a package is already loaded
description:
This might well not be considered a bug, but the output of `library("tidyverse")` includes duplicate  `✔ package` entries if packages from `tidyverse:::core` are already loaded (`tibble` in this instance):

```r
library("ggplot2")
library("tidyverse")
#> ── Attaching packages ────────────────────────────────────────────────── tidyverse 1.2.1 ──
#> ✔ tibble  1.4.2     ✔ purrr   0.2.4
#> ✔ tidyr   0.8.0     ✔ dplyr   0.7.4
#> ✔ readr   1.1.1     ✔ stringr 1.2.0
#> ✔ tibble  1.4.2     ✔ forcats 0.2.0
#> ── Conflicts ───────────────────────────────────────────────────── tidyverse_conflicts() ──
#> ✖ dplyr::filter() masks stats::filter()
#> ✖ dplyr::lag()    masks stats::lag()
```

This can be fixed by slightly tweaking the `regex` used in the function, like so. I'd be happy to submit a pull request, but I won't be able to do so until this evening.

```r
tidyverse_packages_2 <- function (include_self = TRUE) 
{
    raw <- utils::packageDescription("tidyverse")$Imports
    imports <- strsplit(raw, ",")[[1]]
    parsed <- gsub("^\\s+|\\s+$", "", imports)
    # Original
    # names <- vapply(strsplit(parsed, " +"), "[[", 1, FUN.VALUE = character(1))
    # Updated
      names <- vapply(strsplit(parsed, "( )|(\\n)+"), "[[", 1, FUN.VALUE = character(1))
    if (include_self) {
        names <- c(names, "tidyverse")
    }
    names
}

tidyverse_packages_2()
```

title: cli::symbol$tick causes pandoc to fail during kniting
description:
The unicode checkmarks generated (in [attach.R](https://github.com/tidyverse/tidyverse/commit/c704b28052357230a128d95b7c3381318e45cbb1#diff-bad55cdd46f463abc12ea0917fb6a1dfL6)) during initial attachment of tidyverse will cause `rmarkdown` to fail if pandoc is configured to use pdflatex (I think the default)? Given that the checkmarks are aesthetic only, is it possible to keep the attachment manifest as pure ASCII (a "+" was used prior to the change)?

Quick replication: Given a file `loadTidyVerse.R` with the content:

```R
library("tidyverse")
message("done")
```

... then the command:

```R
library("rmarkdown")
render("loadTidyVerse.R", pdf_document()  )
```

... fails with (presuming pdflatex is used by pandoc):

```
See the inputenc package documentation for explanation.

Try running pandoc with --pdf-engine=xelatex.

```

This is in the context of [RStudio](https://www.rstudio.com/) in [Domino](https://www.dominodatalab.com/), though it's presumably a problem in other contexts. We're looking into switching to xelatex, which to be honest we may need to do for other lurking Unicode characters.

For other readers with the same problem, note also that the issue displays the initially baffling behavior of causing knitr to fail the first time, but succeeds on subsequent tries in the same R session - this is because the manifest with the checkmark is generated only on the initial loading of the library. The second knit attempt will not encounter the ticks and will process the document appropriately.

``` r
#> [21] "rvest"       "stringr"     "tibble"      "tidyr"       "xml2"       
#> [26] "tidyverse"
```
Note the entry for `readxl`.

Fix is to change
```
names <- vapply(strsplit(parsed, " +"), "[[", 1, FUN.VALUE = character(1))
```

to

```
names <- vapply(strsplit(parsed, "\\s+"), "[[", 1, FUN.VALUE = character(1))
```

title: getThemeInfo()$dark can be NA
description:
I haven't been able to reproduce this myself, but per this post in the RStudio Community:
https://community.rstudio.com/t/library-tidyverse-results-in-error-on-r-studio/2642/13

A call to `getThemeInfo()` can return:
```r
$editor
NULL

$global
[1] "Modern"

$dark
[1] NA
```

This results in an error in `text_col`:
```
Error: package or namespace load failed for ‘tidyverse’:
 .onAttach failed in attachNamespace() for 'tidyverse', details:
  call: if (theme$dark) crayon::white(x) else crayon::black(x)
  error: missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed
```

This is clearly a problem with the IDE or the API (and I've filed an [issue](https://github.com/rstudio/rstudioapi/issues/73) with the API as a first step), but seems worth putting a band-aid on it for those that will update tidyverse more than the IDE.

title: library(tidyverse) fails on pre-1.1 versions of RStudio due to lack of getThemeInfo
description:
When loading the tidyverse with `library(tidyverse)` in RStudio 1.0.153, the following error occurs:
```
Error: package or namespace load failed for ‘tidyverse’:
 .onAttach failed in attachNamespace() for 'tidyverse', details:
  call: NULL
  error: Function getThemeInfo not found in RStudio
```
Working backwards, the error occurs in `text_col` when it calls `getThemeInfo`. The function checks to ensure that `rstudioapi` is available, but not whether the version in use has `getThemeInfo` available. This can be isolated as:
```r
tidyverse:::text_col("Hi")
# Error: Function getThemeInfo not found in RStudio
```
Running the command on the same computer in the latest release of RStudio does not generate an error.

title: Intra-tidyverse masking
description:
Is there an order, or a method, of installing the secondary tidyverse packages (hms stringr, etc.) such that they do not mask each other's functions? 

For instance, with my current order, I get hms() masked from hms by lubridate, as_factor() masked from forecats by haven, guess_encoding() masked from readr, and bootstrap() masked from modelr by broom.

If these conflicts are illusory, e.g. the masking functions are identical to the masked functions, a reassuring comment in the tidyverse documentation would be appreciated. 

If the conflicts are real and can not be eliminated by an installation method, then I would put this forward as a feature request: name changes such that tidyverse packages can be installed in any combination and order without masking one another's functions.

title: tidyverse ingest conventions
description:
*The requested brain dump to get this started.*

- Function that reads a `thingy` should be named `read_thingy()`. The opposite, when it exists, should be named `write_thingy()`.
- If it makes sense, return a tibble.
  - Any package that creates tibbles should import tibble, to reduce gotchas around, e.g., the `drop = FALSE` behaviour of `[` or the lack of partial matching on `$`.
  - If `thingy` has no data, return a tibble with 0 rows and 0 columns.
- Don't have row names.
- `col_names` is the tidyverse answer to `header = TRUE`. Either logical indicating that first row gives variable names or character vector of names.
- Don't mess with column names, i.e. don't modify non-syntactic names. Exceptions:
  - Fill in missing column names.
  - De-duplicate column names.
- Don't coerce character to factor, `stringsAsFactors = FALSE`.
- Do guess column types *under what circumstances? according to what rules?*
  - Provide control over how much data to use for the guessing, `guess_max = min(1000, n_max)`*
  - Recognize dates and date-times, for some universe of default formats. *And always convert to POSIXct?*
- `col_types` is the tidyverse answer to `colClasses`. There is an entire system for type specification, with short codes or more general "collectors".
  - *consider readr's "problems" and printed/returned colspec*
- *something about locale*
- *something about UTF-8 encoding*
- Explicit control over rows to skip, unrelated to the data: `skip = 0, n_max = Inf`.
- Control over rows (or parts thereof) to skip, based on the data
  - `comment`
  - a vector of `NA` values. Use `quoted_na` to specify what happens to `"NA"`.
- *Something about empty rows/columns. Proposal: include and fill with NA when leading (and not explicitly skipped) or embedded. Treatment of trailing empty rows/columns will depend on context (e.g. possible to include with readr, impossible with readxl).*
- *something about reading from file, compressed file, URL, connection, memory*
- *something about chunked reading*
- whitespace trimming?
- progress?
- Recommendations for implementation? Or a package?

title: add working build settings for travis with packrat + tidyverse
description:
I'm using the standard packrat settings for Travis (container based infrastructure), and I've run into some build problems stemming from `tidyverse` dependencies:

- [this](https://github.com/hadley/readxl/issues/176) for `readxl`, 
- and [this](https://github.com/wesm/feather/issues/154) for `feather`.

Both are related to C/C++ compiler dependencies if I understand the problem correctly.
I'm not sure whether they are related.

I thought I'd post this here because the `packrat` + `tidyverse` + Travis toolchain is perhaps commonly used.

I was also wondering whether it would be possible to publish/recommend a `.travis.yml` that we can rely on to work with the current version of tidyverse dependencies.

Figuring out these dependencies one-by-one is quite cumbersome for people not versed in compiler stuff (like myself), and this might (perhaps?) help **strengthen (technical) reproducibility** around the `tidyverse` toolchain, if it comes with *one* build environment.

Ps.: does this problem arise only when `packrat` is used, or are non-packrat setups used as well?

``` r
tidyverse_conflicts()
#> Conflicts with tidy packages ----------------------------------------------
```


jsonlite then purrr: we learn that `purrr::flatten()` masks `jsonlite::flatten()`.

``` r
library(jsonlite)
library(purrr)
#>

#> The following object is masked from 'package:jsonlite':
#> 
#>     flatten
```

title: feature request: tidyverse_load()
description:
I would really appreciate a function like this:

``` r
#' Load all tidyverse packages.
#'
#' Load all tidyverse packages, separated by type.
#'
#' @param vector loads stringr, forcats, hms and lubridate.
#' @param model loads broom and modelr.
#' @param import loads DBI, haven, httr, jsonlite, readxl, rvest and xml2.
#'
#' @export
tidyverse_load <- function(vector = c('stringr', 'forcats', 'hms', 'lubridate'),
                           model = c('broom', 'modelr'),
                           import = c('DBI', 'haven', 'httr', 'jsonlite',
                                      'readxl', 'rvest', 'xml2')) {
  pkgs <- c(vector, model, import)
  vapply(pkgs, library, character.only = TRUE, logical.return = TRUE, logical(1))
  invisible()
}
```

I didn't make a PR because i think it needs some improvements (invisible loading, better documentation etc). Any thoughts?
